claims.text: Machine learning–assisted process design can achieve comparable densification at lower temperatures than conventional high-temperature sintering.
Machine learning–assisted process design can preserve microstructural control while lowering the sintering temperature.
Historical experimental data and simulation outputs can be used by an ML algorithm to optimize heating ramp rates, dwell times, and peak temperatures.
Optimization of the sintering schedule can lower the required peak sintering temperature.
Optimized heating profiles maintain proper grain-boundary formation during lower-temperature sintering.
Optimized heating profiles maintain phase stability during lower-temperature sintering.
Maintaining grain-boundary formation and phase stability enables densification without abnormal grain growth.
Maintaining grain-boundary formation and phase stability prevents unwanted phase changes.
An ML model can identify nonlinear relationships between sintering parameters and densification outcomes.
Lower peak temperatures combined with tailored heating ramp rates can promote sufficient atomic diffusion and bonding.
Sufficient atomic diffusion and bonding at the optimized lower temperature produce a microstructure comparable to conventional high-temperature sintering.
The ML-optimized protocol will yield density similar to that obtained by conventional sintering.
The ML-optimized protocol will yield microstructural characteristics similar to those obtained by conventional sintering.
The ML-optimized protocol can reduce furnace temperature by an estimated 10–20%.
The approach is applicable when sintering densification mechanisms are well represented by existing experimental and simulation data.
The approach may be less successful in systems with poorly understood sintering behavior.
Highly variable starting-material properties may limit the success of ML-optimized sintering.
